task: T4: document the evidence channel in docs/ and in the header comment block of `scripts/ralph-log.sh`. There is no `--help` to extend — `run-loop.sh` carries only a usage string in a parameter default — and these scripts document themselves in the comment block at the top of the file, which is where a reader of `ralph-log.sh` will look for what it now sends. Say what leaves the worker and when — the prompt, the diff, the gate output, the metadata record and the executor transcript, each at the moment it is written rather than swept up afterwards — and state plainly why it is a push: nothing can connect into a worker, and a run that dies is exactly the run whose evidence matters most, so an artifact that has not already left is one nobody will ever read. Document the configuration as the same two variables the status channel uses, and say that with no URL set nothing is sent and nothing is printed. Document the cap, its override, and what a truncated artifact looks like to a reader. Record what this spec deliberately does NOT do: it does not store, index, retain or serve anything, and the coordinator that receives these artifacts and decides how long to keep them is a separate piece of work. Change no executable behaviour: this task adds documentation and comments only, and an unconfigured run must still be exactly the run it is today.
